claim: For \(L_\alpha=-\Delta+|x|^{2\alpha}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge3\) and \(\alpha>0\), the critical radius satisfies \(\rho_\alpha(x)\asymp(1+|x|)^{-\alpha}\) and \(i(\rho_\alpha)=\alpha\). For \(0<\theta<1/(1+\alpha)\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), the symbol \(b_{\gamma,\beta}(x)=(1+|x|)^\gamma[\log(e+|x|)]^\beta\) belongs to \(\mathrm{BMO}^{\log}_{\rho_\alpha,\theta}(\mathbb R^n)\) if and only if \(\gamma<\theta\), or \(\gamma=\theta\) and \(\beta\le0\). In this membership region, the published endpoint theorem yields bounded commutators \([b_{\gamma,\beta},R_j^{L_\alpha}]\) on \(H_{L_\alpha}^1(\mathbb R^n)\), where \(R_j^{L_\alpha}=\partial_jL_\alpha^{-1/2}\); no boundedness claim is made outside the membership region.
integrity: Analytic estimates and parameter boundaries are derived in the result. The commutator consequence is attributed to the cited theorem. No independent audit or external validation is claimed.
scientific_limitations: The classification is restricted to \(V_\alpha(x)=|x|^{2\alpha}\), \(n\ge3\), \(\alpha>0\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(0<\theta<1/(1+\alpha)\).
No conclusion is made about commutator boundedness outside \(\mathrm{BMO}^{\log}_{\rho_\alpha,\theta}\).
The general commutator theorem is prior work; the contribution is the explicit necessary-and-sufficient family classification and its application.
title: Exact power-log growth threshold for localized BMO symbols
